about: Priors for the true win rate (bb/100, net of rake) estimated from real hands. Read by the live calculation (server/bankroll_posterior.js) and the research code (src/bayes.py, case study chapter 2). Copied from reports/real-hands/q3/results.json, made by research/real-hands/analyze_q3.py; tests/test_real_hands.py checks the copy. The hands themselves are not in this repository.

source.data: PartyPoker and Ongame no-limit hold'em, $2/$4, 1–23 July 2009, HandHQ logs
source.citation: Kim (2024), Recording and Describing Poker Hands, arXiv:2312.11753
source.method: Hierarchical Normal model (empirical Bayes): each player's observed win rate ~ Normal(true win rate, standard error^2), true win rates ~ Normal(mean, sd^2), fitted by maximum likelihood within each volume bracket. Standard errors from each player's own per-hand standard deviation.
source.population: Players with at least 1,000 usable hands at one site in the 23 days; IDs are per site

regulars.label: Regulars, $2/$4 2009: Normal(+2.6, 2.5²)
regulars.population: Players with 10,000+ hands in the 23 days

players.label: Players with 1,000+ hands, $2/$4 2009 (mixture)
players.population: Players with 1,000+ hands in the 23 days, weighted by player

later_minus_earlier_half.about: Each player's hands split in time order into two halves, fitted separately; later minus earlier mean, bb/100

regulars_prediction.about: Predict each regular's later half from the earlier half; squared error relative to using the earlier-half win rate as it is, and coverage of 95% predictive intervals
